newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian farmers hold back soy stocks, arrivals fall.
newsitem.headline: Indian farmers hold back soy stocks, arrivals fall.

text.p: Indian soybean arrivals have slowed to a trickle as farmers hold back stocks to sell later at higher prices, traders said on Tuesday.
"Farmers are holding back stocks for getting better prices in the future," said Gopal Agarwal, a leading oilmeal broker.
Traders said soybean arrivals were around 3,000 tonnes per day compared to 8,000 tonnes a month ago and around 20,000 tonnes at the same time last year in central Indian markets.
Traders said poor arrivals had forced some soymeal processing firms to remain idle.
Prakash Vohra, a leading oilmeal broker, said only 60 percent of all soybean processing plants were in operation as a result.
Traders said soybean was quoted at around 10,900-11,200 rupees per tonne compared to 8,900-9,200 rupees at the same time a year ago.
Export demand was dull and Indian soymeal exporters had signed contracts for only 5,000 tonnes in the past two weeks.
"Export demand was poor and offerings were also limited," said another oilmeal broker.
Traders said Indian exporters have so far contracted to export around 1.5 million tonnes of soymeal in 1996/97 (November-October).
Soymeal export prices were currently ruling at $270-$271 per tonne FAS (free alongside ship) compared to $269 per tonne a month ago and $228 a year ago, traders said.
